correctness.rationale: Finite exhaustive source-code computation reconstructs all 280 distinct unitals by nonsingular Hermitian forms and independently by three nonconcurrent-line symmetric differences. Both verify all 23,520 containing six-sets have 64 traces, five-incidence multiplicity two, six-incidence multiplicity one, and support counts. From any shattered set, its positive trace forces containment; seven points cannot be shattered since their first six uniquely determine a containing unital. Every contained set of size at most six extends to a six-set with all 64 traces. Double incidence counting gives the stated polynomial and complements give the two facet types; domains and boundaries are explicit and finite.

originality.rationale: The published 280-unital construction and code-incidence representations are credited, not claimed new. Comparable material concerns the larger linear span of incidence vectors, the noncollinear cap complex, union-of-two-lines and affine-flat queries rather than the 280-vector membership family; these distinctions are by quantifiers and concept sets, not titles. value.rationale: The 280 Hermitian unitals are a standard, highly symmetric finite-geometric incidence system. It is mathematically nonautomatic that every six-point subset lying in a unital realizes all 64 Boolean patterns across precisely the 280 unitals, whereas every contained seven-set fails. This yields a sharp complete face classification, unexpected pure top-layer uniformity and distinct collinear/noncollinear complement types. It is an exact incidence/design and binary-projection benchmark beyond a routine count of geometric objects, with no claimed unproved all-field extension.
